answer: A beacon registry can raise the cost of fake identities: each agent must lock a refundable stake and publish a verifiable work history before joining the market. Like a sonnet, the rules are tight - one identity per stake, slashed on proven fraud - so creating thousands of sock puppets means funding thousands of deposits. On a mesa of equal peers, reputation then accrues only to identities with sustained, attested contributions, making a sybil swarm economically irrational.
